fix.head: 4a41e70e17db095794ec4817f64bc0178cd93b68
fix.summary:
AGSVC-1 (agent-service), models/agent_models/service.py:213-235 - Wrong logic replaced: the reap was scoped to the three checks only (`try: _wait_healthy/_check_model/_check_render` / `except BaseException: terminate...raise`, with `_write_endpoint_file(...)` and `raise SystemExit(proc.wait())` outside the guard at old lines 228-232), so an OSError from the net-disk endpoint write left the vllm server running with no owner - the python parent dies, the tmux pane closes, and teardown_services' `tmux kill-session` finds no session whose process group it could signal. Right logic: `_write_endpoint_file` and `raise SystemExit(proc.wait())` moved inside the try, and the `except BaseException` handler replaced by a `finally` that reaps when the child is still running (`if proc.poll() is None: terminate / wait(60) / kill / wait`). This is the verdict's corrected_fix, not the finding's proposed except-wrap: it states the rule once and positively - the process started at the Popen is ended before serve() returns by any route - instead of routing the success path through a failure branch. The normal exit is untouched (measured: the server's return code 7 survives, no terminate). No VERSION bump: VERSION 1 in this file, and the change alters no output of any setting, only what happens to a child on a failure route.

F1 (trainer-autocast), models/probe_models/base.py:96-112 - Wrong logic replaced: `attention_mask = batch["attention_mask"].to(device)` moved the mask device-only. The three methods build the packed additive mask float32 (train/methods/cgen.py:137,167-169, ctool.py:122,151-153, cparam.py:164,194-196) and never cast it, while train/utils/trainer.py:69-73 runs every train / validate / predict forward under `torch.autocast("cuda", bfloat16)`, so a float32 [B,1,L_pad,L_pad] bias sat on the card for the whole forward and SDPA allocated its own bfloat16 copy of it beside the original. Right logic: the mask crosses onto the card in the dtype the forward computes in - `torch.get_autocast_dtype(device.type)` when autocast is on for that device, the weights' dtype (`next(self.backbone.parameters()).dtype`) otherwise - and the cast happens before `.to(device)`, so the float32 copy never reaches the card. This is the one place every method's mask crosses, and it reproduces the old trainer's rule (legacy/pipeline/train/train_causal_share.py:254 `mask_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if amp else torch.float32`, shipped at :159) without the per-call-site dtype argument. The integer [B,L] mask of a reference_loss batch is left alone by `is_floating_point()`. The alignment gate keeps comparing in float32: it runs outside autocast (train/utils/trainer.py:408-420) with float32 weights (every probe row in models/table.yaml is `dtype: float32`), so `param.dtype` is float32 there.

VERSION question on base.py, decided by the rule block at base.py:16-25 ("bump only when some existing setting would now produce a different output of a stage that lists this file"): no bump, VERSION stays 2 and VERSION_HISTORY is unchanged. Reason: the mask carries only 0.0 and -inf, both exact in bfloat16, and autocast already handed SDPA a bfloat16 copy of exactly those values - measured in this venv, SDPA under bfloat16 autocast gives a bit-identical result for a float32 mask and for the same mask pre-rounded to bfloat16 (max abs diff 0.0). The alignment gate's float32 pass is unchanged, and the eval/serve path never sees a floating mask (Probe.score and Probe.generate tokenize their own integer mask). So no stage's output changes; the fix is resident and transient device memory only. This follows the verdict's corrected_fix and overrides the finding's proposed_fix, which asked for a bump with `stale: ("train",)`.

README.md was not touched: neither file changed what it imports, reads or writes, and `run.py selfcheck` is green (31 files, 0 problems).

minors.title: base.py comment names a route that cannot carry a floating mask: "the served probe's bfloat16 load"
minors.detail: New comment at models/probe_models/base.py:100-106 (line 103) says the mask crosses in "the weights' dtype everywhere else (the alignment gate's float32 pass, the served probe's bfloat16 load)". The served probe never reaches Probe.forward: models/probe_models/service.py:150 and :158 call score_probe.score(...) and gen_probe.generate(...), and Probe.score (base.py:120-135) and Probe.generate (base.py:137-159) tokenize their own integer [B, L] mask and call self.backbone / self.backbone.generate directly, bypassing forward. A bfloat16-loaded probe is also the only case where load() takes no row (base.py:213-215 falls back to qwen.DTYPE), and no packed-mask caller does that: train/methods/{ctool,cgen,cparam}.py are the only producers of the float [B,1,L_pad,L_pad] mask and they run through train/utils/trainer.py, which restores with the model row (dtype float32 in models/table.yaml:31,37,43). So the parenthetical asserts a code path the tree does not have; the honest pair is the alignment gate's float32 pass alone (train/utils/trainer.py:404-422, which the _bf16_forward docstring at trainer.py:71-72 already describes). Same overstatement sits in the verdict's corrected_fix text ("it also fixes the served probe ... where today a float32 mask would be converted inside every SDPA call too"), so it was carried over rather than introduced by the fixer. Nothing executes differently; this is a fact-discipline defect in a comment. Separately and even smaller: the citation "(contracts 6.2)" is attached to the sentence asserting the additive [B, 1, L_pad, L_pad] shape, and contracts 6.2 (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:3747) pins only the Batch key names, with no shape and no dtype.

minors.title: teardown_launch kills work-piece sessions by name that this launch never started
minors.detail: `failed()` (jobs/launch.py:1071-1074) passes the whole `placed` list to `teardown_launch`, and `teardown_launch` (jobs/launch.py:666-673) kills every non-service piece by its recorded `(host, session)`. At two of the four exits the loop pieces have not been started at all: the service-wave exits at jobs/launch.py:1088 and 1091 and the `service_check` exit at 1101 all run before `_start_wave(loop_pieces)` at 1103. A session carrying one of those names at that moment therefore belongs to an earlier incarnation, not to this launch. The same holds on the new `_start_wave` failure path: its own docstring (jobs/launch.py:388-394) says a `tmux new-session` that fails on a duplicate name means "this launch has no process of its own for that piece" and calls it "somebody else's session" -- and the caller then kills exactly that session. So the docstring claim "End every session this launch started (8.1)" (jobs/launch.py:654) is wider than what the code does: it ends every session the plan *names*. Reachability is narrow, because the new live-piece refusal in run.py (2003-2009) stops the walk whenever meta.json lists a live `loop`/`train` piece and `piece_alive` matches a bare session name from any host (jobs/launch.py:203-219 with jobs/registry.py:492-509). It needs a run directory whose meta.json no longer names the live session -- a meta.json that does not parse takes `_read_meta_or_recover`'s fresh default (jobs/registry.py:198-...), which drops the earlier piece list. Consequence in that state: a running trainer or loop piece is killed with no record, instead of the old behaviour of adopting its session.

fix.head: 977210d
fix.summary:
F1-a (jobs/registry.py) — fixed at the cause, not by narrowing the window.

Wrong logic replaced: jobs/registry.py:1069 (old) `if done.get("finished_at", "") >= start["t"]:` — a comparison between two `_now()` stamps that are both minute-resolution (`_now` at jobs/registry.py:81, `finished_at` at :255, the start row's `t` from run.py:1908-1931), so a stale `done.json` sharing a minute with the open start row passed and sync appended an `ok` row carrying the previous computation's counts, metrics and report onto the launch in flight. The reviewer is right that the two remedies they considered (seconds on `finished_at`, or the done.json mtime against the start minute plus one) are either useless or a trade, and that both other exits (second-resolution start rows, the three `_parse_t` copies, 8.1's row format) lie outside the allowed files. A third exit does not: neither stamp can answer "which launch wrote this file", so the file now carries the answer instead of a time.

Right logic written in its place:
- jobs/registry.py:248-254 — new `_launch_ordinal(run_dir)`: the length of `meta.json`'s append-only `launches` list (8.3). Every launch extends that list in the same lock hold that appends its start row (run.py:1931-1937 for a CPU stage, jobs/launch.py:868-879 for a card stage), so the ordinal identifies the launch exactly, with no clock in it.
- jobs/registry.py:271 — `write_done` stamps `"launch": _launch_ordinal(run_dir)` into `done.json`, beside `finished_at`; its docstring (jobs/registry.py:256-267) states why the field is an ordinal and not a time. No caller changes: the four stage programs and run.py's pair-stage writer get the field from inside `write_done`.
- jobs/registry.py:1078-1089 — the sync test is now `if done.get("launch") == _launch_ordinal(run_dir):`, with the comment rewritten to 8.2 + 8.3. The previous computation's file carries the launch before this one, so it leaves the run open for its own finish row or for the dead-piece test; a `done.json` written before this field existed belongs to no open launch, which is what the review's item (a) asks for.
- README.md:305 — `jobs/registry.py`'s `reads:` line now names `done.json` beside `meta.json` (sync reads it; `write_done` now reads `meta.json`, already listed).

No VERSION bump: `jobs/registry.py` carries no VERSION, and no stage's output changes — `done.json` gains a field that feeds no key.

eval/utils/probe_eval.py and eval/score_run.py: unchanged. The finding names neither, and both get the new stamp through `registry.write_done`.

Verified on a scratch runs.jsonl and run directory (the repo's jobs/runs.jsonl was never opened; script at /tmp/claude-12114/-home-y-guo-reproduce-new1/54da0555-0a40-4cf8-b8c1-72bfb652a6f7/scratchpad/check_sync_gate.py): with start1, the `ok` row, start2 and the previous `done.json` all stamped "2026-09-20 16:40", sync appends nothing and returns []; after the second computation writes its own `done.json` (launch 2) sync returns ['eval-abc'] and the finish row carries that computation's metrics {'coverage@0.05': 0.83}; a `done.json` with the field deleted leaves the run open.

Ordering assumption, theoretical: for a CPU stage run.py spawns the process (run.py:1912) before it appends the `launches` entry (run.py:1937), both inside one lock hold. A child that wrote `done.json` within those microseconds would stamp the previous ordinal and read as stale, leaving the run open for the dead-piece test. A build/eval/score process cannot start its interpreter, read its inputs and finish in that window, and the failure direction is the safe one (no fabricated `ok` row).

minors.title: _launch_ordinal's docstring states an invariant that jobs/launch.refire breaks
minors.detail: jobs/registry.py:248-254 justifies the mechanism with "`meta.json`'s append-only `launches` list (8.3), which every launch extends by one entry in the same lock hold that appends its start row", and the commit message repeats it. That is false as merged: `jobs/launch.refire` appends a `launches` entry through `registry.write_meta(run_dir, pieces=[updated_piece], launches=[launch_entry])` (jobs/launch.py:996) and appends no start row at all — which is exactly finding registry-fold-and-references/F2 in the same JSON ("refire relaunches a piece without appending a start row"). Contract 8.3 (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:4527) says the list holds "one entry per launch **or refire**". The mechanism still works, because all it needs is that the ordinal increases at every relaunch and that writer and reader call the same function, but the stated reason for trusting it is wrong, and a reader checking the invariant against jobs/launch.py:996 will conclude the gate is unsound. The honest statement is "every launch and every refire extends the list, so the ordinal never repeats across relaunches". (If F2's fix lands on another branch and refire starts appending a start row, the sentence becomes true; today it is not.)

minors.title: A recovered corrupt meta.json resets the launches list, so the ordinal restarts and a stale done.json matches again
minors.detail: `_read_meta_or_recover` (jobs/registry.py:197-212) renames an unparseable `meta.json` aside and returns `_default_meta()`, whose `launches` is `[]` (jobs/registry.py:191). The ordinal is therefore not monotone across that recovery: a directory whose previous computation wrote `done.json` with `launch: 1`, whose `meta.json` is then scrambled and recovered, and into which a relaunch is started, has `_launch_ordinal(run_dir) == 1` again, so `done.get("launch") == _launch_ordinal(run_dir)` at jobs/registry.py:1089 passes and sync closes the launch in flight with the previous computation's counts, metrics and report — the exact F1 failure. The repo treats a scrambled `meta.json` as a real event (8.3 at notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:4548-4552 and the recovery function exist for it), and the one-writer-per-file argument there is about truncation, so the compound is reachable, not hypothetical. A counter that survives the recovery (for instance seeding the fresh default from the highest `<launch>` in `heartbeat/<piece>-<launch>.jsonl`, which `beat` at jobs/registry.py:304-319 already resolves that way and which the recovery does not touch) would close it. Low probability; noting it because the whole point of the new field is that the gate cannot be fooled.

minors.title: eval/score_run.py gains a guard no verified finding asks for, against a state the verifier ruled unreachable
minors.detail: The diff rewrites eval/score_run.py:179-190 to check `base_dir is not None and (base_dir / "settings.yaml").exists()` before `load_frozen`. F5's `file` is eval/utils/probe_eval.py alone, its `proposed_fix` says "right after line 599", and its `verdict.corrected_fix` lists two adjustments, both in probe_eval.py. The verdict's reasoning explicitly excludes this file: "the other three `referenced_run_dir` callers are safe — eval/score_run.py:182 (`baseline.sample`) ... all take keys that are in the launched stage's own upstream map and have already passed run.py:1826-1838". I confirmed that: `baseline.sample` is in score's upstream tuple (experimental_settings/schema.py:309) and `_refuse_missing_upstream` (run.py:1826-1838) exits on a None directory before the stage starts. The change is harmless — it turns a `TypeError`/`FileNotFoundError` into a named `ValueError` — but it is scope the branch was not given, in a file whose only mandate here was F5, and it adds a check for a condition run.py already refuses. The branch's first commit (3624bd6) attributes it to F5, which the JSON does not support.

minors.title: Contracts 8.2 and 1.5 now describe a rule the code no longer implements, with no errata entry
minors.detail: 8.2 (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:4489-4492) still prescribes the time rule — "`run.py` appends a new finish row whenever `done.json`'s `finished_at` is later than the newest finish row for that `run_id`" — and 1.5's table (line 1404) still gives `done.json` as `{stage, key, commit, finished_at, counts, versions, metrics, report}` plus `pairs`/`stage_extra`. The merged code compares launch ordinals and writes a `launch` field, and 8.2's literal rule is in fact the bug F1 reports (a stale `done.json` is later than the newest finish row precisely in the relaunch case). The review's corrected_fix asked for the chosen rule to be "state[d] in the errata so 8.2's sentence and the code agree"; no errata entry was added. The fixer disclosed this in the 977210d commit message as out-of-allowed-files work for the main session, so it is a handoff item rather than a hidden gap, but as merged the code cites 8.2 in jobs/registry.py:1078 and :257 for a rule 8.2 does not state, and the next reader of the contract will reach the wrong conclusion.
